disease_label_per_paper: Acute West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease (West Nile meningoencephalitis) in a 61-year-old man with multiple comorbidities
presentation_summary: 61-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, prior stroke, COPD, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, thyroid nodule/goiter, on clopidogrel and apixaban, presented to the ED with 5 days of black stools and fever progressing to profuse diarrhea, fever, and chills, with intermittent sharp lower abdominal pain; he was confused on presentation.
He denied nausea, vomiting, sick contacts, and recent tick bites. Four days earlier he had an ED visit for similar symptoms with mild hyponatremia (Na 130).

Admission labs: Na 126, K 4, creatinine 0.76 mg/dL, BUN 7 mg/dL, glucose 165 mg/dL, calcium 8.2 mg/dL, albumin 3.1 g/dL, AST 140 U/L, ALT 73 U/L, WBC 4.4 x10^3/uL, TSH 0.25 uIU/mL; orthostatic hypotension; head CT without acute changes.

post_presentation_workup_record.finding: Brain MRI (hospital day ~2): chronic encephalomalacia left frontal and parietal lobes from prior stroke, no acute changes
post_presentation_workup_record.source_text_value: Initial MRI of the brain revealed areas of encephalomalacia in the left frontal and parietal lobes and evidence of previous stroke but no acute changes

post_presentation_workup_record.finding: EEG (hospital day 3): moderate encephalopathy with continuous generalized slowing
post_presentation_workup_record.source_text_value: EEG revealed moderate encephalopathy due to continuous generalized slowing, which was nonspecific in etiology

post_presentation_workup_record.finding: Lumbar puncture (hospital day 4): clear CSF, opening pressure 36 cm H2O, CSF WBC 140/mm3 per Table 1 (text states 59) with 47% neutrophils and 47% lymphocytes, CSF glucose 128 mg/dL, CSF protein 197 mg/dL
post_presentation_workup_record.source_text_value: Lumbar puncture was done at the bedside, with clear liquid collected. The opening pressure was 36. ... There was leukocytosis of 59 with a differential indicating 47% neutrophils and 47% lymphocytes; CSF glucose 128; CSF total proteins 197; CSF WBC 140

clinical_course_record.finding: Hospital day 2: altered mental status and hypoxia requiring emergency intubation; second-degree heart block after propranolol
clinical_course_record.source_text_value: On the second day of admission, our patient had a rapid response for altered mental status and hypoxia, requiring emergency intubation. Subsequently, the patient was found to have a second-degree heart block following the propranolol dosing

clinical_course_record.finding: Hospital day 3: intubated, unresponsive to verbal and noxious stimuli off sedation, no nuchal rigidity, sluggish pupils, absent corneal reflexes; chest X-ray left lower lobe consolidation (possible hospital-acquired pneumonia) with small effusion
clinical_course_record.source_text_value: He remained unresponsive to verbal and noxious stimuli ... There was no nuchal rigidity. ... Corneal reflexes were absent. ... Chest X-ray revealed left lower lobe consolidations secondary to possible hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) with a small, associated pleural effusion.
On the fifth day of admission, the patient developed supraventricular tachycardia

clinical_course_record.finding: Hospital day 8: new right arm weakness; repeat MRI punctate restricted-diffusion foci along occipital horns; cervical spine MRI negative
clinical_course_record.source_text_value: At the time of diagnosis, our patient was having increasing right arm weakness with flexion ... Repeat MRI showed a punctate lesion in the occipital horn

confirmatory_findings.finding: CSF West Nile virus IgM positive (4.59), IgG negative (<1.30) on hospital day 8
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Subsequent testing for fungal antibodies showed no detection of the cryptococcus antigen, but confirmed WN with IgG values <1.30 and IgM values at 4.59.

confirmatory_findings.finding: CSF PCR negative for VZV, CMV, enterovirus; CSF cryptococcal antigen negative; other meningitis microbes negative; tick panel and Monospot negative
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Spinal tap testing for viruses revealed negative results for varicella-zoster virus, cytomegalovirus, and enterovirus per PCR testing. ... Monospot testing was negative.

confirmatory_findings.finding: BAL Gram stain yeast and gram-positive cocci (hospital-acquired pneumonia work-up)
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Gram stain of the BAL showed some yeast and gram-positive cocci.

actual_treatment: meropenem, vancomycin, acyclovir, then ampicillin and ceftriaxone

outcome.source_text_value: Three days post PEG tube placement and one day post tracheostomy, our patient was accepted and transferred to a long-term care facility.

quality_warnings: Snapshot is hospital day 0 (presentation). No quantitative vital signs are reported at presentation; the quantitative presentation evidence is laboratory data (11 values).

Brain MRI (day ~2), EEG (day 3) and CSF analysis (day 4) are recorded as post-presentation work-up and are non-ranking in this presentation-stage case; the loader also does not consume observations dated after snapshot_day.
CSF WBC is internally inconsistent in the paper (Table 1: 140/mm3; text: 59).
Day -4 sodium (130) from the prior ED visit is structured as a dated observation.
Hospital-course complications (intubation, heart block after propranolol, hospital-acquired pneumonia, SVT) and WNV serology are non-ranking.
